ownerSource.exactText: it sounds like you figured out a real flaw in how github work is done. make sure you send that lesson over to mission control chat.

exactIssue: A one-shot GitHub Actions workflow can correctly mutate and clean a task branch yet leave the resulting github-actions[bot]-authored PR head with required pull-request workflows reported as terminal failure/action-required placeholders containing zero jobs. Treating workflow-run labels alone as semantic CI results is unsafe. Separately, canonical reconciliation invalidated tests that had accidentally coupled historical fixtures and proposal-state assumptions to the live graph, and hard-coded inventory literals drifted after legitimate graph growth.

botHeadFacts: Verify, workflow policy, and CodeQL workflow runs were terminal failure/action-required-style placeholders on the bot-authored head.
The corresponding required-workflow runs had zero jobs, so they were not substantive test failures.
A subsequent human-authored no-semantic-change commit triggered the protected checks normally on the exact same final tree lineage.

secondaryLessons: Canonical reconciliation changes authority state; proposal tests must transition from pre-reconciliation materialization assertions to post-reconciliation canonical regression assertions.
Historical immutable packet tests must validate their archived graph/source bundle rather than rebuilding the historical packet from current live authority.
Inventory assertions such as graph node/edge counts must be updated as part of legitimate reconciliation and should not masquerade as semantic therapy failures.
Expensive historical fixture rebuilds inside the general protected gate can create runner-liveness failures; immutable fixtures should be reused when the test is not specifically testing the builder.
A one-shot workflow must remove its own workflow/script before the final authority head is approved; temporary reconciliation machinery must never land on main.
proposedChange: Mission Control should gate GitHub completion on the exact final tree/head and inspect required check-runs/jobs, not workflow-run conclusion strings alone. Add a final-head liveness rule: after any automation/bot-authored self-cleanup mutation, confirm temporary machinery is absent, distinguish zero-job bot placeholders from substantive CI failures, ensure the exact final tree receives real required checks, and merge only after those exact-head checks are green. Reconciliation workflows should also classify test failures as semantic regression versus lifecycle/inventory/fixture coupling before modifying product semantics.

risks: A blanket rule that rejects every bot-authored final commit would be too broad; the actual invariant is substantive required checks on the exact final tree.
A synthetic human-authored no-op commit should be a compatibility fallback, not the preferred architecture if GitHub can be made to run checks correctly on the automation-authored head.
Do not infer semantic product defects from inventory or historical-fixture lifecycle failures.
workerRecommendation: Add this as a Mission Control GitHub execution/reconciliation guard and a hostile regression fixture. The controller should automatically classify zero-job required-workflow placeholders, verify temporary-workflow cleanup, request or create a legitimate final-head check trigger when needed, and refuse merge until the exact final tree has substantive green required checks.
workerUncertainty: The exact GitHub platform cause of the zero-job bot-authored PR workflow placeholders is not proven here. The observed behavior and the required fail-safe handling are proven by the execution trace.
decisionThatCanChange: Mission Control GitHub completion detection, one-shot workflow handling, reconciliation closeout, and protected-branch merge admission.
